 From Hotels To Hospitals: UIDAI Brings 300 Entities Into Aadhaar's Paperless Verification System, App Nears 7.5 Crore Downloads
 Swarajya Staff
 Nov 06, 2026 | Updated 04:18 PM GMT+5:30
 Save & read from anywhere!
 Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app .
 Sign In Prefer Prefer Aadhaar (Pic Via Wikipedia) The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) has onboarded 300 Offline Verification Seeking Entities (OVSEs) since the programme's rollout in January, marking a significant expansion of India's paperless identity verification ecosystem. 
 The development enables organisations across multiple sectors to verify Aadhaar details without collecting physical copies of documents.
 The expansion covers sectors ranging from hotels, hospitality, healthcare, education, events, gig economy and consumer-facing players.
 The move is expected to reduce the collection of physical Aadhaar copies as ID proof, addressing a practice that is not permitted under the Aadhaar Act.
 The offline verification mechanism enables secure, consent-based and paperless verification, empowering both service providers and residents.
 The onboarding of these OVSE partners reflects growing confidence in Aadhaar-enabled, privacy-first digital verification frameworks that prioritise user control while ensuring ease of access and data minimisation in alignment with the provisions of DPDP Act.
 Complementing the institutional expansion, the Aadhaar App continues to gain traction, with nearly 7. 5 crore downloads recorded so far. 
 The Ministry of Electronics and IT confirmed that 86.37 lakh mobile number updates, 22.16 lakh address updates and 40.25 lakh email updates have been completed through the app, allowing residents to update their details without visiting an Aadhaar centre.
 Additionally, 3.61 lakh Aadhaar lock and unlock transactions have been carried out through the app. 
 UIDAI stated that the framework prioritises privacy, user control and data minimisation in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, whilst the expansion supports the government's Digital India vision.
